children: is taking steps to protect itself financially if a massive New Mexico data center is delayed, sending a force majeure notice to the project's developer as concerns build around the execution risks behind the AI infrastructure boom. The notice does not necessarily mean the project is in trouble, but it highlights how schedule slippage at multibillion-dollar facilities can ripple across tenants, lenders and suppliers.
The facility, known as Project Jupiter, is being developed by Stack Infrastructure, a portfolio company of Blue Owl Capital. Oracle is the main tenant.

According to Bloomberg, Oracle wants to defer payments if the site misses its planned 2028 opening. It remains unclear whether the force majeure notice would release Oracle from any existing financial obligations.

The market reaction was immediate. Oracle shares fell about 4% in premarket trading, while Blue Owl dropped roughly 4%. Bloom Energy, whose fuel cells are expected to help power the site, fell 5%, and SoftBank shares declined about 6%.
Project Jupiter is designed for 2.45 gigawatts of capacity, making it one of the larger facilities tied to the broader Stargate AI infrastructure buildout involving Oracle, OpenAI and SoftBank.

The project's financing also raises the stakes. About 20 banks provided an $18 billion loan to support development of the campus, meaning any extended delay could affect more than just Oracle's occupancy timeline.
For Oracle investors, the main issue is execution risk rather than an immediate change to the company's AI demand story.
The key questions are whether Project Jupiter still comes online in 2028, whether Oracle's payment obligations shift, and whether delays force the company to seek alternative compute capacity.
Investors should also watch for any knock-on effects across Stargate-linked projects, financing costs and Oracle's capital commitments.

If the notice proves precautionary and the project remains on schedule, the market reaction could fade. But broader delays would raise questions about whether AI infrastructure expansion is moving faster than power, financing and construction systems can realistically support.

title: Oracle Flags Fresh Risk for Massive AI Project
